title: 어딜 가, 거제도?  (Go Where? Geoje Island?)

segments.t: In a flashback to Ra Joon-mo's revamped travel show starring veteran actresses, screen legend Youn Yuh-jung flatly vetoes a long trip down south and sleeping outdoors. Listen for how she says 'I can't go' and 'it's cold'.
봄맞이 특집으로 거제도를 갑니다.
어딜 가? 거제도? 나 못 가.
왜 멀리만 가려고 그래?
그리고 야외 취침이야, 이게?
멀리 간다고 시청률 나오는 거 아니야.
봄이라 그러지 마, 지금 추워 죽겠어.
시청률이 사실 지금 좀 바닥이에요.
위기는 기회니까 그렇게 불안하지 않아요.
Let's walk through the eight lines of Joon-mo's tough outdoor shoot.
봄맞이 특집으로 거제도를 갑니다.

It literally means this. 'For our spring special, we're going to Geoje Island.' The opening phrase literally means a special broadcast episode welcoming spring. Geoje is a scenic southern island hours from Seoul This literally means that.
어딜 가? 거제도? 나 못 가.

It literally means this. 'Go where? Geoje Island? I can't go.' As a respected elder speaking to a younger director, Yuh-jung uses crisp casual speech to ask 'go where?', then places the negation word for 'cannot' right before the word 'go' to state flatly 'I cannot go' The word doubles the.
왜 멀리만 가려고 그래?

It literally means this. 'Why do you keep trying to go so far away?' She attaches the word for 'only' onto 'far away' to complain that he only ever picks distant spots, then ends by asking 'why are you trying to go?' This literally means that.
그리고 야외 취침이야, 이게?

It literally means this. 'And is this sleeping outdoors?' Fans of Korean travel shows know this classic variety-show punishment by heart—sleeping outdoors for the night, usually inside a chilly tent! It is a handy word.
멀리 간다고 시청률 나오는 거 아니야.

It literally means this. 'Going far away doesn't make ratings come out.' She uses a connective ending to challenge a false assumption—'just because you travel far doesn't mean...'—and pairs 'ratings' with an expression meaning 'that's not how they come out' Notice the word for.
봄이라 그러지 마, 지금 추워 죽겠어.

It literally means this. 'Don't call it spring, I'm freezing to death right now.' Koreans constantly add 'I could die!' right after word like 'cold', 'hungry', or 'tired' for everyday dramatic emphasis It comes from this.
시청률이 사실 지금 좀 바닥이에요.

It literally means this. 'Honestly, our ratings are at rock bottom right now.' Back in his interview chair, Joon-mo admits the numbers hit the 'floor'—literally 'rock bottom'—while softening the painful truth with words meaning 'in fact' and 'kind of' We built from this.
위기는 기회니까 그렇게 불안하지 않아요.

It literally means this. 'Crisis is opportunity, so I'm not that anxious.' Putting on a brave face, he quotes the classic proverb pairing 'crisis' with 'opportunity', then cleanly negates the word for 'anxious' This short for that. Now let's listen to the whole Geoje Island flashback again.
봄맞이 특집으로 거제도를 갑니다.
어딜 가? 거제도? 나 못 가.
왜 멀리만 가려고 그래?
그리고 야외 취침이야, 이게?
멀리 간다고 시청률 나오는 거 아니야.
봄이라 그러지 마, 지금 추워 죽겠어.
시청률이 사실 지금 좀 바닥이에요.
위기는 기회니까 그렇게 불안하지 않아요.
You picked up how to say 'I can't go', an expressive phrase for when it's freezing to death, and the proverb 'crisis is opportunity'. Back to the meeting room next!
안녕!

lines.fragment: 멀리 간다고 시청자 오는 거 아니야
몸이라 그러지 마 지금 추워 죽겠어
근데 또 위기는 기회니까 그렇게 불안하지 않아요
